name: Biomedical Sciences Interdisciplinary PhD Program
summary: Interdisciplinary PhD in biomedical sciences at Tulane School of Medicine. Students complete at least three lab rotations in the first year before choosing a dissertation advisor.

deadlines.label: Priority deadline
deadlines.note: Applications opened September 1, 2026; admissions are on a rolling basis.

timeline.interviews: Interviews are offered to the most competitive candidates and begin in January; the Admission Requirements page says they run from January through March.

english.note: Normally required for the PhD if English is not your native language; applicants with lower scores are evaluated on their complete package. Waived for applicants with a degree from an institution where instruction was in English.

documents: Official transcripts from all prior colleges or universities
Credential evaluation for degrees from outside the US
requirements.note: There is no application fee. GRE or MCAT scores are not required but are evaluated if provided.

funding.note: The program page says PhD students receive a stipend of approximately $35,000 per year (no year stated) for the entire program, usually four to seven years, plus a full tuition waiver and paid health insurance. PhD students from outside the US receive the same financial package as US citizens.

international.note: About one third of incoming PhD students are international. Foreign credentials must be evaluated even when instruction was in English.
